paper_metadata.title: Association of acute depressive symptoms and functional connectivity of emotional processing regions following sport-related concussion

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a well-defined sample of NCAA Division I student-athletes with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and a matched control group. The recruitment source and baseline characteristics are thoroughly described.

items.reasoning: Only 44% (19/43) of the concussed sample completed all three visits, which is relatively low for a longitudinal study.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (functional connectivity) was measured using standardized 3T MRI protocols and rigorous preprocessing (motion censoring, regressing white matter/CSF signals). The use of a meta-analytically derived network reduces bias in ROI selection.

items.evidence_snippet: functional connectivity was calculated in a meta-analytically derived network of regions associated with emotional processing.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined as Fisher-Z transformed correlation coefficients between 23 specific ROIs.

items.evidence_snippet: Resting state fMRI data was collected on a 3 T scanner (TR = 2 s)... Time points with volume-to-volume head motion > 0.30 mm were censored
items.reasoning: The study uses standard high-field MRI and applies rigorous motion correction and censoring to ensure data quality.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement

items.evidence_snippet: Imaging data were collected on a General Electric Healthcare Discovery MR750 3-Tesla whole body scanner
items.reasoning: All participants were scanned using the same equipment and protocol.
